en: The Sūtra on the Prediction of the Fruit for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, translated by the Tripitaka Master Huijian of the Song Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Kapilavastu in the Śākya country.
In the Nyagrodha Garden at Śrāvastī, he was observing the *varṣā* (rainy season retreat) together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī went to where the World-Honored One was; having arrived, she prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One and stood to one side.
Having stepped back to stand to one side, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī addressed the Blessed One, saying: "Venerable Sir,
is it possible for a woman to attain the four fruits of the ascetic life?"
"Would you allow women to go forth from home into homelessness out of faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya,
abandoning their households to study the Path? "Stop, Gotamī!"
"It is not necessary.
Women may not, within this Dharma and Vinaya, go forth with faith and joy, renounce the household life, and study the Path. You, Gotamī!"
"One should always shave one's head and wear the *kāṣāya*, and until the end of one's life, practice the pure *brahmacarya*.

Thereupon, the great woman Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, having been thus instructed by the World-Honored One, prostrated at the World-Honored One’s feet, circumambulated him, and departed from the World-Honored One’s presence.
At that time, the bhikṣus were making robes for the Blessed One, as the Blessed One was soon to go to Śrāvastī to observe the rainy-season retreat (*varṣā*).
Having completed the retreat and finished making the robes during the three-month period, he set out on tour among the human settlements, carrying his robes and bowl.

When Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī heard that the bhikṣus were making robes for the World-Honored One, and that the World-Honored One would soon go to Śrāvastī to observe the rains retreat, and that after completing the three-month retreat he would finish his robes and travel among the people together with his bowl and robes; she [acted accordingly].
Having heard this, the great woman Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī went to where the World-Honored One was. Upon arrival, she prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the great woman Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

Is it possible that a woman may attain the four fruits of asceticism, and that a woman, out of faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya, may go forth from the home life, renounce the household, and train in the path?
"Stop, Gotamī! There is no need for this."
Women should not, within this Dharma and Vinaya, take pleasure in going forth from the home life, abandoning their households to study the Path.
You, Gotamī! Having shaved your head and donned the saffron robes, practice the pure Brahma-faring until the end of your life.
Thereupon, the Great Woman Gotamī, having been twice rebuked by the Blessed One, paid homage at the Blessed One’s feet, circumambulated him, and departed from his presence.

At that time, the Blessed One was observing the rains retreat at Śrāvastī. Having completed the retreat and finished his robes during the three-month period, he set out on a journey through the human realm, carrying his robe and bowl.

The Great Woman Gotamī heard that the World-Honored One was observing the rains retreat at Śrāvastī; having completed the retreat and finished making robes during the three months, he set out with his robe and bowl to travel among the villages of men.
Having heard this, the Great Lady Gotamī, together with many elderly women, followed behind the World-Honored One.
As they followed behind the World-Honored One, he traveled by stages until he reached Nāḍika and stayed at the Āpaṇa hall in Nāḍika.
At that time, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī went to where the Blessed One was; having arrived, she prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Having stood to one side, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī addressed the Blessed One, saying: "Venerable Sir!..."
Is it possible for a woman to attain the four fruits of śrāmaṇya?
Is it possible for a woman, out of faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya, to go forth from the household life, renounce the home, and train in the path?
"Stop, Gotamī! There is no need for this."
Women may not go forth from the household life into homelessness to study the path within this Dharma and Vinaya. Gopikā!
Shave your head, don the saffron robes, and practice the holy life with ultimate purity until the end.
Thereupon, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, having been refused three times by the Blessed One, prostrated at the Blessed One’s feet, circumambulated him, and departed from his presence.
At that time, the Great Lady Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī stood before the gate, her feet unwashed, her body covered in dust, her eyes dazed and vacant, weeping.
From afar, the Venerable Ānanda saw the Great Lady Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī standing before the gate with unwashed feet, her body covered in dust, her eyes dazed and vacant, and weeping;
having seen this, he spoke these words: "For what reason, Gautamī?"
"Why has he not washed his feet? His body is covered in dust, he is dazed and weary, and he stands weeping before the gate?
"It is so, Venerable Ānanda."
"Women cannot attain this Dharma and Vinaya; they cannot with faith and joy go forth from the household life, renounce their homes, and train in the path.
"Stay here, Gotamī; I shall go to where the Blessed One is, and having arrived, I shall inform the Blessed One."
Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda went to where the Blessed One was; having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and withdrew to stand to one side.
Having withdrawn to stand to one side, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"Venerable Sir! Blessed One!"

Is it possible that a woman might attain the four fruits of śrāmaṇya, and that a woman might, out of faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya, go forth from the home life, renounce the household, and train in the path?
“Stop, Ānanda! There is no need for this.
Women may not, within this Dharma and Vinaya, go forth with faith and joy, renounce the household life, and train in the path.”
"Ānanda! If women were to go forth in this Dharma and Vinaya—going forth out of faith and joy, abandoning their homes to train in the path—the holy life (brahmacariya) would not endure for long."
"It is just as if, Ānanda, there were a household with many women and few men; would they likely have many offspring?
"No, [World-Honored One]."
"Yes, World-Honored One!
"It is so, Ānanda! If women were to go forth in this Dharma and Vinaya—leaving home out of faith and joy, abandoning their homes to study the Path—the holy life would not endure for long."
It is just as, Ānanda,
when a field of rice or a field of barley has been cultivated, if hail or rain should fall upon it in the interim to its detriment, that hail or rain will cause it to perish because of it.
Thus it is, Ānanda!
If women, having faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya, go forth from the household life to leave home and study the Path, the holy life (brahmacarya) cannot endure for long.
“Yes, World-Honored One!
The Great Lady Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has been of great benefit.
When the World-Honored One’s mother passed away, she was the one who raised him by nursing him with her milk.”
“Just so, Ānanda! Just so, Ānanda!
This great woman Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī has been of great benefit; when my mother passed away, she nourished me with her milk.”

"Ānanda! I too have greatly benefited Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī; she has relied upon me, taken refuge in me, taken refuge in the Dharma, and taken refuge in the Saṅgha of bhikṣus. She is without doubt regarding the Buddha, without doubt regarding the Dharma, without doubt regarding the Saṅgha, and without doubt regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path."

Endowed with faith, ethical discipline, learning, and generosity, and endowed with wisdom, they abandon killing and abstain from killing; they abandon taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and false speech, up to abandoning the drinking of intoxicants and abstaining from the drinking of intoxicants.

Ānanda! Suppose there is a person who, relying upon others, takes refuge in the Buddha, takes refuge in the Dharma, and takes refuge in the Saṅgha of bhikṣus; who has no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha; who has no doubt regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; who is fully endowed with faith, ethical discipline, learning, and generosity, and is fully endowed with wisdom; and who abandons killing and abstains from killing, abandons taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and false speech, up to abandoning the drinking of intoxicants and abstaining from the drinking of intoxicants.
"In this regard, Ānanda!

Whatever one might do for such a person—providing them with clothing, bedding, seats, and medicines for their illness throughout their entire life—one could not repay that person's kindness. Furthermore, Ānanda!"
Women, Ānanda, should establish eight weighty rules which women must not transgress, and which women should observe throughout their entire lives.
It is just as follows, Ānanda!
Just as a skilled disciple of a master diver, having entered deep water, spreads a net therein, guarding the water and cutting it off so that it does not flow away; even so, Ānanda!
Women should practice the eight weighty rules (gurudharma), which women must not transgress; women should maintain these precepts for as long as they live.
What are the eight?
"In this regard, Ānanda!
A bhikṣuṇī must seek full ordination from a bhikṣu. This is it, Ānanda!"
I have established for women the first weighty rule, so that women shall not transgress it, and so that women shall maintain their precepts until the end of their lives. This, Ānanda!
A bhikṣuṇī must receive the ritual salutation from a bhikṣu every half-month.
This, Ānanda, is the second heavy rule I establish for women, which women must not transgress and which they shall observe together with their precepts for as long as they live.
"In this regard, Ānanda!
If there is no bhikṣu present, a bhikṣuṇī must not perform the *varṣā* (the rains retreat ceremony).
It is for this reason, Ānanda!"
I have established three fundamental rules for women, so that women may not transgress them and may remain endowed with the precepts throughout their lives.

Ānanda! When a bhikṣuṇī reaches the time for the *varṣā* (rainy-season retreat), she must do so together with both Saṃghas, performing the *varṣā* ceremony through the three matters of what has been seen, heard, and known.
This, Ānanda, is what I have established as the four grave rules for women, which women must not transgress and with which they must remain until the end of their lives.
In this regard, Ānanda!
If a bhikṣu does not grant permission, a bhikṣuṇī may not question the bhikṣu regarding the Sūtras, the Vinaya, or the Abhidharma;
thus it is, Ānanda!
"If monks grant permission, a bhikṣuṇī shall question a monk regarding the Sūtras, the Vinaya, and the Abhidharma. This, Ānanda,
is what I establish as the five heavy dharmas for women, which women must not transgress, and with which women shall remain until the end of their lives."
In this regard, Ānanda!
A bhikṣuṇī must not revile a bhikṣu based on what she has seen, heard, or known; Ānanda!
"A bhikṣu may criticize a bhikṣuṇī based on what he has seen, heard, or known. Ānanda,
this is the sixth heavy rule (gurudharma) I establish for women, which women must not transgress and with which they must remain throughout their lives."
"Ānanda! If a bhikṣuṇī has committed an offense of saṃghāvaśeṣa, she must sweep and sprinkle for two assemblies for half a month.
This, Ānanda, is [the rule]."
I have established seven weighty rules for women, so that women shall not transgress them, and so that women shall maintain these precepts until the end of their lives. Ānanda!
If a bhikṣuṇī has been fully ordained for even a hundred years, she must prostrate at the feet of a bhikṣu who has just received full ordination, and she must serve him with reverence.
This, Ānanda, is what I have established as the eight weighty rules for women, which women must not transgress, and with which they must remain throughout their entire lives.
Thus it is, Ānanda! For women, I have established these eight weighty rules, which must not be transgressed by women, and with which they must remain throughout their lives.
"Ānanda! This great lady Gotamī,
provided she abides by these eight weighty rules, shall train in this Dharma and Vinaya and receive full ordination as a bhikṣuṇī."

Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda, having heard what the Blessed One had said, reflected upon it well, recited it, and took it up for practice; he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed from the Blessed One’s presence to return to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.
Having arrived, he spoke these words to Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī: "It has been granted, Gautamī!
Women may, within this Dharma and Vinaya, with faith and joy, go forth from the home life, renounce their households, and train in the path."
"Gautamī! The Blessed One has spoken thus:
'The eight weighty rules must be observed; a woman may not transgress them, and for as long as her life lasts, she must remain in accordance with these precepts.'"
"What are the eight? Gautamī!
A bhikṣuṇī must seek to receive full ordination from a bhikṣu."
This, Gotamī, is the first heavy rule established by the Blessed One for women, which women must not transgress, and with which they shall remain throughout their lives.
"Go, Gautamī! Even if a bhikṣuṇī has been fully ordained for a hundred years, she must approach a fully ordained bhikṣu, prostrate at his feet, and pay him respectful homage."
Thus it is, Gotamī! The Blessed One has established these eight weighty rules for women, which women must not transgress, and with which women shall remain until the end of their lives.
Thus it is, Gotamī! The Blessed One has established these eight weighty rules for women, which women must not transgress, and with which women shall remain until the end of their lives.
"Kṣemā Gautamī! One who is able to abide by these eight weighty rules shall train in this Dharma and Vinaya, receive full ordination, and become a bhikṣuṇī."
"So it is, Venerable Ānanda! Listen to a parable from me.
One who possesses wisdom understands its meaning upon hearing the parable. It is just as if, Venerable Ānanda!"

Whether she be a Kṣatriya woman, a Brāhmaṇa woman, a woman of the artisan class, or a woman of the commoner class, having bathed thoroughly and anointed herself with fragrant scents and wearing pure white garments, there might be someone who, out of compassion and wishing to benefit her or bring her peace, gives her a garland of *utpala* flowers, or a garland of *campaka*, *vārṣika*, or *atimuktaka* flowers; she would receive it with both hands and place it upon her head.
"So be it, Venerable Ānanda!
I shall receive these eight weighty rules established by the Blessed One with my head bowed, for as long as I live. "You, Great Woman Gotamī!"
"You should train in this Dharma and Vinaya, receive full ordination, and become a bhikṣuṇī.

Thereupon, the great woman Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, at a later time, together with a community of elder bhikṣuṇīs and accompanied by the most venerable senior bhikṣuṇīs, practiced the holy life and went together to where the Venerable Ānanda was.
Having arrived, she prostrated at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda and stood to one side.
Once the Great Lady Gotamī had stood to one side, she addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"Venerable Ānanda!..."

When these bhikṣuṇīs are senior elders who have all practiced the holy life (brahmacarya), and these bhikṣus are newly ordained, having not long since begun their study of the Path and not long since entered this Dharma and Vinaya, these bhikṣus should treat these bhikṣuṇīs as elders; they should pay them homage and serve them.
"Stop, Gotamī! I shall go to where the Blessed One is, and having arrived, I shall report these words to the Blessed One.
Now, follow Venerable Ānanda.
Thereupon, the Venerable Ānanda went to where the Blessed One was; having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and withdrew to stand to one side.
Having withdrawn to stand to one side, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One, saying: "Yes, Blessed One!"

Today this great woman, Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī, together with the bhikṣuṇīs—who are all venerable elders and have all practiced the holy life—came to where I was; having arrived, she prostrated at my feet and stood to one side.
After Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī had stepped back to one side, she said to me:

"Venerable Ānanda, you should know that these bhikṣuṇīs are senior elders who have all practiced the holy life (brahmacarya). These bhikṣus, however, are newly ordained, having not long studied the Path and not being long in this Dharma. You should cause these bhikṣus to behave toward these bhikṣuṇīs as they would toward elders, and as elders, they should pay them homage and serve them."
"Stop, Ānanda! You must guard these words; do not speak such words again. You, Ānanda!"
"You should know that according to what I understand, not even a single phrase can be explained; how much less could one speak such words? Ānanda!

If women were not to go forth from the household life out of faith and joy in this Dharma and Vinaya to practice the path as renunciants, then brahmins and householders would spread their robes upon the ground, and having spread their robes upon the ground, they would say: [This is for her]."

"These śramaṇas possess virtuous conduct; these śramaṇas should practice the higher path. These śramaṇas are most wonderful in their diligence; we shall obtain meaningful benefit throughout the long night."

"O Ānanda! If women had not, out of faith and delight in this Dharma and Vinaya, left the home life for homelessness to train in the path, then brahmins and householders would have spread their hair upon the ground and said:

'Let the śramaṇas walk upon it; let the śramaṇas stand upon it. The śramaṇas' conduct of the precepts is exceedingly difficult; we shall thereby obtain benefit and profit throughout this long night.'"
"Ānanda, if women had not,

out of faith and delight, gone forth from the home life into homelessness to train in this Dharma and Discipline, then Brahmins and householders would have been on the road carrying various bags filled with goods,
saying: 'O worthy ones!'"
"You should accept this food and drink at your pleasure; by doing so, we shall obtain benefit, profit, and peace for a long night.

Ānanda, if women had not, out of faith and delight, gone forth from the home life into homelessness to train in this Dharma and Discipline, then the brahmins and householders would have placed their trust in the virtuous conduct of those śramaṇas, and they would have embraced them with their hands, brought them into their own homes, and provided various offerings, saying: "Take and use these as you please, O Worthy Ones; thereby we shall obtain benefit, profit, and the happiness of peace for a long night."
"In this regard, Ānanda!

If women had not, out of faith and delight, gone forth from the home life into homelessness to train in the path within this Dharma and Vinaya, then even though the sun and moon possess such great majesty and power, the radiance of those śramaṇas who practice the precepts would surpass them; how much more so, then, could it surpass that of the corrupt and evil followers of other teachings?"

Ānanda! If women had not, out of faith and joy, gone forth from the home life into homelessness within this Dharma and Vinaya to practice the path, the legacy of the Teaching would have remained for a thousand years; now that five hundred years have already passed, five hundred years remain.
"Ānanda! This is impossible;
it cannot be admitted that a woman will ever attain these five things:
she cannot become a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha; nor can she become a Wheel-turning King (Cakravartin); nor can she become Śakra, nor Māra, nor Brahmā—this is impossible."
It is possible for a man to attain five things:

it is possible for him to become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; it is possible for him to become a Wheel-turning King (Cakravartin); it is possible for him to become a Śakra, a Māra, or a Brahmā. Such a thing is indeed possible.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
Having heard what the World-Honored One had said, the Venerable Ānanda rejoiced and was glad.
This is the *Sūtra on the Prediction of the Fruit for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī*.
